findings.title: Rollback mutates an existing installation on an unadmitted target without a native preview token
findings.trigger: An existing installation has a rollback generation, then the current OS/WebView/Profile/resources are no longer admitted. A main-view caller invokes plugin_package_rollback with its installId. The handler accepts no preview/approval token and does not inspect authority.policy()/target admission before invoking rollback_package.
findings.effect: The native rollback succeeds and changes the selected generation and permission epoch despite the preview-only target boundary. Runtime rollback can also replace the namespace with the verified previous data. Hiding the renderer rollback port is insufficient to reject this still-permitted main-view IPC. Runtime does disable the installation and clear grants; this evidence does not demonstrate external execution or permission restoration on an unadmitted target.
reproduction: Test-only admit an independent temporary PluginAuthority and install unsigned-store twice through native previews/commit_preview.
Set that authority's admission false to model a changed/unaccepted target; verify both execution modes are denied and no preview remains.
Invoke authority.with(runtime.rollback_package(installId, PackageFiles)) exactly as dispatched by control.rs.
Expect rejection without state mutation. Actual result is success with generation/epoch changed, causing the negative assertion to fail.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Add a native rollback preview/confirmation bound to the verified retained candidate and current installation/epoch. Consume its opaque single-use token, check current target policy before any mutation and reject stale or unadmitted requests. Preserve verified recovery, monotonic epochs and grant clearing. Add permanent regressions for unadmitted targets, stale/replayed confirmation and an admitted explicitly approved rollback.
